extraction_metadata.purpose: Assess complexity of migrating this Oracle 19c PL/SQL system to a target platform

overall_complexity.rationale: RC-009 CORRECTED (DA Agent 2): Prior score 'HIGH' understated the cumulative burden. VERY HIGH is warranted by: (1) Oracle Forms 4.x UI — the dominant effort item, no automated migration path, full rewrite required (~40 days alone); (2) 11 PL/SQL packages (~3,000-4,000 lines) with 6+ Oracle-specific APIs (UTL_FILE ×4, UTL_SMTP, DBMS_CRYPTO, PRAGMA AUTONOMOUS_TRANSACTION, CONNECT BY); (3) 2 CRITICAL blockers before migration can begin (broken authentication stub, hard-coded encryption key requiring live-DB decrypt-re-encrypt pass); (4) EMPLOYEE_HISTORY trigger column mismatch that may have already produced corrupt history records; (5) implicit DBMS_SCHEDULER jobs with no DDL to migrate; (6) hard-coded 2024 tax law values that will be stale on day 1. Total rough estimate is 110 days even without UAT or parallel run. Systems at this score routinely run 1.5-2× estimated effort.

complexity_factors.detail: SSN_ENCRYPTED (EMPLOYEES, EMPLOYEE_DEPENDENTS) and ACCOUNT_NUMBER_ENC (EMPLOYEE_BANK_ACCOUNTS) encrypted with Oracle DBMS_CRYPTO. Hard-coded key 'HR$ystem_3ncrypt10n_K3y_2024!!'. Migration requires: (1) decrypt all records in Oracle, (2) re-encrypt with target platform cipher, (3) establish new key management.

VW_ORG_HIERARCHY and PKG_REPORTING use Oracle CONNECT BY syntax for org chart traversal. PostgreSQL equivalent is WITH RECURSIVE CTE; MySQL uses WITH RECURSIVE; SQL Server uses CTE. Behavior for cycles and LEVEL pseudo-column differs across platforms.

PKG_REPORTING.compensation_summary uses ROUND(MEDIAN(sr.BASE_SALARY), 2) to compute median salary per dept/grade/job group. Oracle's MEDIAN() aggregate function has no direct equivalent in PostgreSQL or SQL Server. PostgreSQL equivalent: PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY BASE_SALARY). SQL Server equivalent: PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY BASE_SALARY) OVER (...). If RPT_COMPENSATION is implemented as a materialized table populated by a re-implemented refresh procedure, the median logic must be rewritten. If compensation_summary is rewritten as an application query, the ORM or query layer must use the platform's ordered-set aggregate. NULL handling may also differ: Oracle MEDIAN ignores NULLs; PERCENTILE_CONT behaviour with NULLs varies by platform.

PKG_AUDIT.log_action and PKG_NOTIFICATION.queue_notification use PRAGMA AUTONOMOUS_TRANSACTION. This Oracle-specific directive allows the inner call to commit independently of the caller's transaction. PostgreSQL does not support this natively — requires a separate connection or dblink for the same effect.

4 Oracle Directory Objects used for flat-file integration: GL_FEED_OUT, BENEFITS_FEED_OUT, TIME_ATTENDANCE_IN, PAY_REGISTER_OUT. UTL_FILE is Oracle-specific. Migration requires replacement with OS-level file I/O (e.g. PL/Python in PostgreSQL, stored procedure external file access on SQL Server) or redesign to use S3/SFTP/message queue for external file exchange.

PKG_NOTIFICATION.send_email uses UTL_SMTP to call smtp.internal.company.com:25 directly from the database. Most cloud databases do not allow outbound SMTP from within the DB engine. Migration requires moving email delivery to an application layer (Lambda, Cloud Function, etc.) and replacing direct UTL_SMTP calls with queue-based delivery.

EMPLOYEES.PHOTO_BLOB (BLOB), EMPLOYEES.NOTES (CLOB), PERFORMANCE_REVIEWS (4× CLOB), PERFORMANCE_GOALS.GOAL_DESCRIPTION (CLOB), NOTIFICATION_QUEUE.BODY (CLOB), AUDIT_LOG.OLD_VALUES/NEW_VALUES (CLOB). PostgreSQL uses BYTEA/TEXT equivalents. Bulk migration must handle LOB streaming; LOBs over 2000 chars may need special ETL treatment.

The entire user interface is Oracle Forms 4.x — a technology that cannot be migrated to any non-Oracle platform without a full UI rewrite. .fmb (form definitions), .pll (PL/SQL libraries), .rdf (reports) must be replaced with a web framework. UI migration typically represents 40-60% of total migration effort for Oracle Forms systems.
complexity_factors.notes: Oracle Forms migration is typically the dominant effort item; consider AuraPlayer, PITSS, or full rebuild

complexity_factors.detail: All business logic in PL/SQL. Oracle-specific features used: DBMS_CRYPTO, UTL_FILE, UTL_SMTP, UTL_RAW, SYS_CONTEXT, PRAGMA AUTONOMOUS_TRANSACTION, CONNECT BY. Packages total ~3,000-4,000 lines of PL/SQL. Migration to PostgreSQL requires rewriting in PL/pgSQL (with extensions); migration to a web tier requires extracting into application code.

All sequences use NOCACHE except SEQ_AUDIT (CACHE 100). PostgreSQL uses SERIAL/IDENTITY or CREATE SEQUENCE (supports cache). Mapping is straightforward. Only SEQ_EMP_NUMBER needs special attention due to the MAX()+1 race condition bug that bypasses it.

TRG_EMP_INSTEAD_OF_DELETE is an Oracle BEFORE DELETE trigger that blocks deletes. PostgreSQL supports BEFORE DELETE triggers natively. The column mismatch in TRG_EMP_BEFORE_UPDATE (DQ-006) must be resolved before migration. All trigger bodies use Oracle PL/SQL syntax.

LEAVE_BALANCES.AVAILABLE is an Oracle virtual column defined as OPENING_BALANCE+ACCRUED-USED+ADJUSTMENT-PENDING. PostgreSQL supports generated columns (GENERATED ALWAYS AS ... STORED) in v12+. The exact behavior (stored vs. virtual) and NULL handling must be validated.

complexity_factors.feature: Tax brackets, fiscal year, pay rates hard-coded in packages
complexity_factors.detail: 2024 US federal tax brackets, SS wage base, Medicare rates, standard deductions, and fiscal year (Oct 1 start) are all hard-coded constants in PKG_PAYROLL and PKG_COMMON. These must be extracted to configuration tables before migration to avoid baking stale 2024 values into the migrated system.

PKG_SECURITY.authenticate does not check passwords (DQ-003). Migrating this stub as-is creates a systemically insecure application on the new platform. Authentication must be properly implemented (ideally replaced with OAuth2/OIDC SSO) before or during migration.

Two scheduled jobs (notification queue processor every 5 min; monthly leave accrual) are referenced in comments but no CREATE_JOB DDL was found. The scheduler configuration must be discovered from the live Oracle DB or reconstructed. On migration: replace with pg_cron (PostgreSQL) or cloud scheduler.

migration_effort_estimate.note: Rough order-of-magnitude estimates; actual effort depends on target platform and team familiarity
migration_effort_estimate.total_rough_estimate_note: Does not account for UAT, data validation, parallel run, or rollback planning

migration_blockers: Hard-coded encryption key — must rotate before migration; cannot migrate encrypted data without the key being in the clear during migration window
EMPLOYEE_HISTORY trigger column mismatch — current system may have corrupt history records; audit before migrating
Authentication stub — deploying the migrated system with no authentication is unacceptable; must implement first
Oracle Forms UI — no automated migration path; full UI rewrite required
migration_quick_wins: Schema DDL is clean and standard — table/column structure maps easily to PostgreSQL
Seed data (reference data) is well-structured and easily portable
AUDIT_LOG is self-contained and can be migrated as-is
